routines.semantics: Replaces a caller-owned integer set with sorted kernel-pool frame IDs for classes 2 through 6, -1 selects all pool classes, and class 1 returns an empty set (built-in inertial frames are not pool frames). Invalid classes signal BADFRAMECLASS and insufficient set capacity signals SETTOOSMALL. No ownership transfer. Frame class input must be a signed 32-bit integer; malformed JS values are rejected instead of being truncated/wrapped.

scenarios.observes: kplfrm returns frame IDs defined in the loaded frame kernel for class 4; real raw.kplfrm mutates an allocated integer cell, and every extracted ID/cardinality reaches StepOutput.value.ids. Python calls sp.kplfrm with the same capacity. Error cases require the named SPICE diagnostic from both executions.

routines.edgeAssessment: Live coverage includes all classes (-1), inertial class 1, empty pool, repeated invocation, unloading, invalid class, and zero-capacity overflow. Direct WASM unit coverage additionally prepopulates/reuses cells, checks sorted multiple classes, stale/foreign/wrong-type handles, and post-error successful recovery. Both generated web/Node glue modules execute the compiled export and recover from BADFRAMECLASS. Native direct tests also exercise set replacement, wrong-type and expired handles, capacity and post-error recovery.
routines.errorAssessment: BADFRAMECLASS and SETTOOSMALL are asserted from both live outputs, preventing two unrelated failures from passing. Wrong-type/expired/foreign handles are wrapper ownership errors covered directly in WASM tests. Shared shim resets SPICE errors; unit test verifies failed() is false and a subsequent success works.

fixtures.provenance: Existing baseline repository-authored synthetic FK for fictional TSPICE_PARITY_TOPO relative to J2000; arbitrary frame ID and rotation angles.
fixtures.distribution: Reused unchanged project test fixture; no mission data or new copied scientific dataset. See fixtures/README.md.

routines.fixtureRationale: One existing minimal FK distinguishes nonempty ID retrieval from constant-empty output. Empty-pool and invalid-class cases need no kernels. No new scientific data is distributed.
routines.cleanup: The harness allocates a fresh real integer cell and frees it in finally on success/error. The WASM adapter verifies live per-module cell ownership and frees the error buffer in withMalloc finally. C shim validates registry/type and resets CSPICE errors after failure. Case lifecycle clears pool/error state before/after each workflow; test client disposal runs in finally. Python owns its ctypes cell memory and runs case finalizers. WASM tokens retire only after successful free; private pointers cannot be guessed from Node IDs or revived by allocator reuse. Token issuance occurs before C allocation, including fail-closed exhaustion. Separate host realms retain caller context affinity.
routines.tolerance: IDs and cardinalities are integral and compared as complete sorted sets. At the fixture ID scale, the existing 1e-12 relative tolerance is much smaller than one ID unit; no tolerance change. Direct unit tests also assert exact IDs and lengths.

findings.summary: Raw WASM kplfrm threw; registered scenarios invoked a separate fallback that also rejected valid class -1.
findings.repair: Exported the existing shared C shim through typed/required WASM exports, regenerated both glue targets/shared binary with pinned CSPICE N0067 and Emscripten 3.1.74, added ownership checks, and removed the harness fallback/unsupported policy. Added class/capacity/state/error coverage.

findings.summary: Native kplfrm converted cell handles with Uint32Value, so a fractional value or one offset by 2^32 could alias and mutate a live cell. The new regression failed before the repair.
findings.repair: Use the existing ReadCellHandleArg validator before native cell lookup. Tests forge fractional/wrapped/non-finite handles and assert rejection without changing the real cell.

findings.summary: Non-integral or overflowing class values could silently truncate/wrap before CSPICE; direct native regression failed for 4.5.
findings.repair: Both typed adapters call assertSpiceInt32 before entering CSPICE. Direct Node/WASM tests reject fractional, non-finite, and overflowing class values while valid -1 and unknown integer classes retain their existing semantics.

findings.summary: Later cell audit demonstrated same-address foreign handles and reused expired pointers can pass the shared WASM membership guard, including consumers such as kplfrm. A separate opaque-token lifetime repair is in progress; earlier support/class tests do not certify this misuse boundary.
findings.repair: Issue non-reused host-realm tokens above uint32 before allocating a cell, retain module-local token/pointer maps, and resolve every cell/window argument at the compiled call boundary. Actual backend regressions reject same-address foreign cells, allocator-reused expired cells/windows, invalid frees and foreign arguments across all ten other raw consumers; valid contents remain unchanged.

node.trace: raw.kplfrm -> Node typed adapter -> registered native Kplfrm -> validated cell registry -> tspice_kplfrm -> kplfrm_c.

wasm.trace: raw.kplfrm -> per-module ownership check -> withMalloc error buffer -> typed/required _tspice_kplfrm in regenerated web/Node WASM -> existing shared shim -> kplfrm_c. No harness substitute remains.
